description: The plot illustrates the relationship between Initial Confidence and Accuracy, displaying three distinct metrics. The x-axis is labeled "Initial Confidence" and features a linear scale ranging from approximately 0.87 to 1.00, with numeric tick marks spaced at intervals of 0.01. The y-axis is labeled "Accuracy" and uses a linear scale with visible tick marks ranging from 0.0 to 1.0 at intervals of 0.2, though the data extends slightly above 1.0. The "Final Accuracy" is represented by a solid blue line with circular markers and error bars, showing a steady upward trend across the x-axis; it starts at a value of approximately 0.95 at x=0.87 and rises to approximately 1.2 at x=1.00. The "$\Delta$ Accuracy" is depicted by a dashed orange line with diamond markers and error bars. It begins at approximately 0.3 at x=0.87, experiences a minor local peak of roughly 0.45 at x=0.92, drops slightly to 0.4 at x=0.93, and then steadily increases to end at approximately 0.8 at x=1.00. The "Initial Accuracy" is shown as a dash-dot green line with square markers and error bars. It starts at approximately 0.65 at x=0.87, increases to roughly 1.0 at x=0.90, dips slightly to 0.95 at x=0.91, climbs to a peak of approximately 1.15 at x=0.98, and finally declines to approximately 1.0 at x=1.00.
